questions.prompt: What is the relationship between a PV and a PVC?

options.text: A PVC is a request; a PV is the piece of storage that satisfies it
A PV requests storage from a PVC
They are the same object
A PVC is cluster-scoped, a PV is namespaced

questions.explanation: The PVC is namespaced and belongs to the app; the PV is cluster-scoped and belongs to the infrastructure.

options.text: One Pod may mount it, ever
It may be mounted read-write by Pods on a single node
It may be read once
Only the control plane may write to it

questions.explanation: The boundary is the node, not the Pod. ReadWriteOncePod is the newer mode that really does mean one Pod.

questions.prompt: A PVC bound to a PV with `persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Delete` is deleted. What happens?

options.text: The PV is kept and becomes Available
The PV and the underlying storage are deleted
The PV becomes Released and keeps the data
Nothing

questions.explanation: Retain is the policy that keeps the volume - it goes to Released and needs manual cleanup before reuse.

questions.prompt: A PVC stays Pending. What are the usual causes?

options.text: The Pod has not started
No matching PV exists and no StorageClass can provision one
The namespace is missing
The PVC has no labels

questions.explanation: `kubectl describe pvc` names it: no volume plugin, no matching size or access mode, or a StorageClass that does not exist.

questions.prompt: You increase a PVC's requested size. When does that work?

options.text: Always
Only if its StorageClass sets allowVolumeExpansion: true
Only for ReadWriteMany volumes
Never - size is immutable

questions.explanation: And even then only upwards. Shrinking is never supported.
